logline: A married chaebol couple on the brink of divorce find themselves fighting to save both their crumbling marriage and each other's lives.

bollymeter.basis: Record-breaking viewership, 100% Rotten Tomatoes critical approval, and mass audience devotion balance against Korean film-critic consensus calling it the year's most overrated drama, landing it as a phenomenon with real craft gaps.

pull_quotes.text: Queen of Tears is buoyant and decidedly comic.

seasons.review_body: The numbers are real: 682.6 million hours on Netflix, tvN's all-time viewership record, and Rotten Tomatoes at a clean 100% from six critics. The case against is also real: Cine21's year-end poll crowned it 2024's most overrated K-drama, with critics noting plot-logic holes and tonal whiplash in the back half. The consensus sits somewhere in between. Kim Soo-hyun and Kim Ji-won anchor the show with a chemistry that carries even the most overwrought turns, and director Kim Hee-won keeps the production glossy enough to blur structural seams. The first half runs on sharp comic timing; the second half leans into melodrama and the wheels loosen. By any craft standard, this is a well-produced, star-powered limited series that earned its audience. The Korean film-critic dissent is worth noting, but the room voted with its eyeballs.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.review_body: Queen of Tears Season 1 Episode 1 aired March 9, 2024 on tvN with simultaneous Netflix streaming as the premiere of a 16-episode series that eventually recorded 682.6 million Netflix hours and broke tvN's all-time viewership record. The series earned 100 percent Rotten Tomatoes from 6 critics; IMDb audiences scored it 8.2. NME called it 'buoyant and decidedly comic.' The premiere establishes the show's tonal register with precision: chaebol heiress Hong Hae-in and her farmer-born husband Baek Hyun-woo have a marriage cold on paper, but the episode reveals with comic accuracy that both are more invested than they admit. Kim Soo-hyun and Kim Ji-won's chemistry is immediate and is the primary reason the show's first half plays as compulsively as it does. The premiere's final revelation - Hae-in's diagnosis - reframes the premise from a divorce comedy into something with genuine life-or-death stakes.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Chaebol heiress Hong Hae-in and her farmer-born husband Baek Hyun-woo have a marriage on paper that is cold to the touch - but the premiere reveals, with comic precision, that both are more invested than they pretend. Kim Soo-hyun and Kim Ji-won's chemistry is immediate.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Hae-in's diagnosis - the revelation that reframes the show's premise from a divorce comedy into something with genuine stakes.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 5
episode_reviews.review_body: Queen of Tears Season 1 Episode 5 aired March 30, 2024 on tvN and Netflix as part of the 16-episode series that recorded 682.6 million Netflix hours and earned 100 percent Rotten Tomatoes from 6 critics and IMDb 8.2. NME called the series 'buoyant and decidedly comic.' This episode is the show's funniest extended sequence: a corporate social event forces Hong Hae-in and Baek Hyun-woo to perform a marriage they privately consider over, and Kim Ji-won's comic precision in navigating the gap between public performance and private contempt is the season's best showcase for her range. The episode represents the first half's tonal confidence at its peak - the moment before the series shifts registers into melodrama. Audience and critic response to this episode, within the show's enormous viewership, consistently identified it as the season's most purely enjoyable single hour.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The show's funniest extended sequence - a corporate social event requiring the couple to perform a marriage they privately consider over - gives Kim Ji-won her best comic showcase of the season. The episode represents the first half's tonal confidence at its peak.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The couple's improvised public display of affection that fools everyone except each other.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 10
episode_reviews.review_body: Queen of Tears Season 1 Episode 10 aired April 13, 2024 on tvN and Netflix as part of the 16-episode series that recorded 682.6 million Netflix hours and 100 percent Rotten Tomatoes from 6 critics. IMDb audiences scored the series 8.2. This episode marks the melodrama gear change that Cine21's year-end critics flagged as the season's tonal inflection point: the corporate intrigue escalates and the series asks its leads to carry scenes that depend more on sincere emotion than comic timing. Kim Soo-hyun's ability to play grief and love simultaneously in the same close-up is the primary reason the tonal shift holds - the performance absorbs what the writing's structural seams might otherwise expose. The disclosure of what Hae-in has been keeping from Hyun-woo is played in a single sustained close-up that audience reviews identified as the episode's defining moment.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The melodrama gear change arrives here as the corporate intrigue escalates and the show asks its leads to carry scenes that depend more on sincere emotion than comic timing. Kim Soo-hyun's ability to play grief and love simultaneously is the reason this holds.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Hyun-woo learning what Hae-in has been keeping from him - the episode's pivot, played in a single close-up.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 16
episode_reviews.review_body: Queen of Tears Season 1 Episode 16 aired April 28, 2024 on tvN and Netflix as the finale of a 16-episode series that logged 682.6 million Netflix hours and broke tvN's all-time viewership record. The series earned 100 percent Rotten Tomatoes from 6 critics; IMDb audiences scored it 8.2. Jae-Ha Kim on Substack called the series 'sometimes unwieldy but always entertaining.' The finale resolved a season's worth of corporate conspiracy and personal grief in a manner that satisfied the series' enormous audience even where it strained credulity - the plot-logic critique that Cine21 critics had raised through the season did not prevent the finale from achieving the emotional payoff its audience had invested in. The final scene between Hae-in and Hyun-woo drove large-scale social media response on broadcast and was the most-screenshotted K-drama finale moment of the April 2024 broadcast window.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale resolved a season's worth of corporate conspiracy and personal grief in a way that satisfied its enormous audience even where it strained credulity. The 682.6 million hours on Netflix tell the story of a finale that delivered what it promised.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The final scene between Hae-in and Hyun-woo - 16 episodes of tension paying off in an image that broke social media for two days.

critic_note.text: Sometimes unwieldy but always entertaining, Queen of Tears is already leading the pack for best drama of the year.
